# ADR-056 — Phase 8 is Consolidation and Adoption, not an AI capability phase; no pgvector, no write-capable agent

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Phase 8 is Consolidation and Adoption, not an AI capability phase.** This supersedes the `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` phase-plan entry for Phase 8 only, in the same way ADR-038 superseded Phase 5, ADR-046 superseded Phase 6 and ADR-052 superseded Phase 7. The superseded entry read: *"Phase 8 — AI layer. Semantic search over everything (pgvector), chat with tool access to all modules, proactive surfacing. This is why inbox-first matters — by now everything is uniformly structured and queryable."* That sentence is half true and half false in the way that matters: everything **is** uniformly structured, and almost nothing is in it. **Phase 8 objective: make Personal OS a daily driver.** Goals: make failures visible, reduce capture friction, make stored content findable, make project and source state durable, reduce agent context overhead, and then use the system long enough to collect real adoption evidence. **The evidence this rests on, measured first-hand at Checkpoint 8.0.** The repository is eighteen days old (first commit `fba85f1` 2026-08-15, HEAD `533601c` 2026-09-01, 244 commits, eight phases). Production holds 2 tasks, 3 notes, 6 inbox items, 0 projects, 0 events and 0 occurrences, while health syncs hourly, mail and calendar every fifteen minutes and monitoring every minute — the integrations have data and the user-authored core does not. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` gives exactly one explicit product instruction, *"Live on Phases 0–3 for a month before continuing. Half of what you think you want in Phase 4 will change"*, and it was skipped by **zero days**: Phase 3 Checkpoint 6 closed 2026-08-20 and Checkpoint 4.1 is recorded complete the same day. The near-empty core is therefore treated as the forecast consequence of a skipped soak, **not** as a falsified product thesis, and Phase 8 reinstates the soak rather than building over the emptiness. **Read-only intelligence before write-capable intelligence.** Any future AI lane is read-only first. A write-capable or tool-calling agent is NOT approved by this ADR and requires its own, separately argued decision. The reason is recorded verbatim in `apps/worker/src/mail/digest/prompt.ts`: the only real guarantee the AI layer currently has is that the summarizing lanes have no tools, can write nothing but text and reach no other table, so a fully successful prompt injection produces misleading prose and never an action. A tool that writes voids that guarantee, and a lane that can read `mail_messages` while holding a write tool launders attacker-authored text into an action. Additionally, any future agent must NOT hold the `posops_app` role, which has full DML on all 37 tables including `ai_provider_connections`, `ai_task_routes`, `devices` and every `*_connections` table — an agent on that role could rewrite its own model routing or mint device credentials. **AI privacy posture is hybrid, and is a decision rather than a default: local retrieval and corpus selection when retrieval is needed, bounded cloud reasoning over the selected excerpt.** **Unrestricted full-content cloud egress is NOT approved.** Today the Daily Brief sends a closed scalar allowlist (ADR-043) and the mail digest sends exactly two bounded attacker-controlled fields (ADR-054); nothing else leaves. Widening that to whole note bodies, calendar contents or health values requires an explicit later decision, not an extension of an existing contract. **No retrieval layer is necessary at the observed corpus size.** The entire first-party corpus is roughly 2k tokens against the Brief lane's already-proven 12,000-character ceiling, and everything including mail headers and health rows is roughly 30–40k tokens, i.e. it fits in a single model call several times over. Retrieval buys selectivity over a corpus with nothing to select from, so an embedding or retrieval layer is deferred until measured corpus size or query latency justifies it. Recorded as a fact for whenever that day comes, and verified first-hand rather than assumed: the installed `ai@7.0.66` exports `embed`, `embedMany`, `EmbeddingModel` and `cosineSimilarity`, and all five configured adapter kinds expose an embedding model — which genuinely falsifies the load-bearing reason `resolve-transcription-connection.ts` gives for its near-duplication, so an embeddings lane would be a symmetric sibling of `buildLanguageModel` rather than a rewrite, and would need no schema change. **pgvector is EXCLUDED FROM PHASE 8 and is NOT permanently forbidden.** The Postgres image remains frozen at `postgres:17-alpine`. Phase 8 must prove simpler retrieval alternatives first, and at present data volume a brute-force cosine scan answers the whole corpus in single-digit milliseconds. Future vector infrastructure may be reconsidered only if measured corpus size or query latency justifies it, and **any future Postgres image change requires its own infrastructure ADR and explicit owner approval** — because the image ships no pgvector control file and `posops_app` holds USAGE not CREATE on `public`, so enabling it means replacing the image and therefore recreating the container that the frozen deployment order in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` names as never to be targeted after the Checkpoint 4.7 Gate C incident, under ADR-024's no-backup posture, and it would additionally be a musl-to-glibc collation change under a live data directory. **Migration posture for Phase 8: prefer new tables over widening existing ones, and target zero migrations.** Verified first-hand in `packages/db/scripts/reconcile-drizzle-tracking.ts`: `CREATE TABLE` is probed for existence only, so a new table may declare any column type; the five-type allowlist (`text`, `bytea`, `date`, `timestamptz`, `timestamp`) binds only `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`, so an ordinary `ADD COLUMN ... boolean`, `integer`, `uuid`, `jsonb` or `numeric` aborts the reconcile script even though all of those types are already used inside `CREATE TABLE` elsewhere; and any index method other than btree aborts, which makes a GIN or tsvector index fail by the identical code path as HNSW. Search in Phase 8 is therefore query-time and index-free. **AI lane placement principles, recorded before any lane is built.** The codebase has already answered this question two different ways and justified the split circularly: `POST /briefs` generates synchronously inside `apps/api` and returns the artifact (ADR-041/043), while `POST /mail-digests` returns 202 and explicitly cannot say a digest exists, justified at `apps/api/src/routes/mail-digests.ts` by where the pipeline code was put rather than by a property of the work. Both are one bounded `generateText` call under identical 30s/45s budgets. The principles: a read-only lane that must answer a user synchronously belongs in `apps/api`; any lane that is scheduled, retryable, fan-out or externally rate-limited belongs in `apps/worker`; `apps/api` must never import from `apps/worker`, and entity creation from a model tool call lives only in `apps/worker/src/commit-parsed-entity.ts`, so a lane needing both synchronous response and domain writes is a design that must be argued explicitly rather than discovered during implementation. **Every new notification producer must carry a per-occurrence dedupe discriminator** — a date, an incident id, or an occurrence id — never a bare long-lived entity id. `notification_dispatch_log.dedupe_key` is a permanent PRIMARY KEY with no TTL and no sweep, so a key scoped to an entity id fires exactly once in the system's lifetime and is then permanently dead, silently, with the job completing successfully. This is a written rule rather than a remembered one because it has already cost a real missed production alert. **Explicitly preserved and unchanged by this ADR: ADR-018** (Tailscale-only, no public ingress of any kind — no webhook receiver, no Pub/Sub push endpoint, no Funnel, no hosted metrics scrape); **ADR-024** (no database backup system; note that a git remote and an encrypted copy of a configuration file are not a database backup system and do not reopen it); and **ADR-046** (Apple HealthKit and Android Health Connect remain removed from scope entirely — additionally over-determined because `eas.json` declares no `ios` block and `app.config.ts` declares no `bundleIdentifier`, so no iOS build can be produced). **Phase 8 checkpoints:** 8.0 foundation, record compaction, ledger reconciliation and source durability (documentation only) · 8.1 make failure visible and make the Brief lane safe to receive externally-authored text · 8.2 enable the real calendar · 8.3 query-time search and export · 8.4 capture front doors · 8.5 instrumented adoption soak with a feature freeze · 8.6 decide on evidence. **No Phase 8 runtime, API, worker or mobile deployment may occur until Checkpoint 7.9 is formally closed** (Phase 8 Checkpoint 8.0, user-approved 2026-09-02)
